lq.ANSWER:
1. Definition and Use of Higher-Order Function (4 marks)

A higher-order function takes other functions as arguments or returns a function.
It promotes modular design by allowing flexible logic without changing the function structure.

2. Python Program with Custom Higher-Order Function and Lambdas (6 marks)

def apply_grading(scores, grading_func): return [grading_func(score) for score in scores] scores = [85, 70, 45, 90] # Convert to grades grades = apply_grading(scores, lambda x: 'A' if x >= 80 else 'B' if x >= 60 else 'C') print("Grades:", grades) # Add bonus bonus_scores = apply_grading(scores, lambda x: x + 5 if x > 80 else x) print("Bonus Scores:", bonus_scores)

3. Benefits of Lambdas and Functional Idioms (5 marks)

  • Lambdas provide quick, in-place logic without defining full functions.

  • Functional idioms like mapping functions keep code concise and readable.

  • Help create flexible, reusable, and testable code for real-world problems.
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
You are building a student grading system. The system receives a list of student scores and must apply different grading policies dynamically, such as:

  • Converting marks to grades (A, B, C, etc.).

  • Adding bonus marks to high-performing students.

  • Applying penalties for low attendance.

Your lead developer recommends using custom higher-order functions and lambda expressions to make the system modular and concise.

Task:

  1. Define a higher-order function and explain how it helps modular design. (4 marks)

  2. Write a Python program that defines a custom higher-order function to apply different grading logics using lambda expressions. (6 marks)

  3. Explain how using anonymous functions (lambdas) and functional idioms improves flexibility in problem-solving. (5 marks)
